summary: Tested iter-26 in-app support messaging end-to-end. Backend: 19/19 pytest cases passed (thread auto-create, user→admin message + unread increment, admin inbox, admin reply + user unread, mark-read for both roles, PATCH close (admin-only + non-admin 403), cross-user isolation (GET messages, POST messages, attachment fetch), body validation (empty/>5000), attachment upload + retrieval + content-type/size validation). Frontend: non-admin SUPPORT tab fully working — tab visible, SupportThread renders, send message round-trips and renders the new bubble. Admin: bubble correctly NOT rendered, header admin-support-link navigates to /admin/support, AdminSupportInbox lists threads, clicking inbox-thread loads SupportThread with messages, inbox-toggle-close button is present and clickable.

ui_bugs.issue: Preview-environment 'Made with Emergent' badge (#emergent-badge) is positioned at viewport bottom-right and overlaps two product UI elements: (1) the floating support bubble toggle at bottom-right, and (2) the SEND button on the chat input row in /admin/support. In automated testing without force-click the badge captures the click. In real user use the badge will still partially cover/obscure the bubble. Recommend bumping z-index on .fixed bottom-6 right-6 button and the chat-input-row send button container above the Emergent badge, OR shifting the bubble to bottom-6 right-24 (or use bottom-left) so the two elements don't collide.

action_items: Resolve overlap between Emergent preview badge and floating support-bubble + admin chat SEND button (z-index / position adjustment).
Confirm on production deploy where the Emergent badge is absent that no other element overlaps the bubble.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/support.py is 363 lines — well structured. Excludes _id from responses. Good use of unread counters on both sides.

Attachment data stored as base64 inside Mongo doc — fine for an MVP (5MB cap), but storing many large attachments will inflate the support_messages collection and slow list queries (list endpoint already projects out attachments.data_b64, which is the right call). Consider moving to GridFS or external object storage if usage grows.
PATCH endpoint allows admin to change subject and status, but no audit log of who closed the thread / when. Consider stamping closed_at + closed_by_admin_id for future support analytics.

post_message reopens any closed thread on every new message (status:'open' in $set). Good for re-engagement but may surprise admin who explicitly closed a thread and then sends a follow-up message themselves — admin reply will reopen it. Probably intentional; just noting.

_notify_email runs await asyncio.wait_for(send_html_email(...), timeout=10) INSIDE the POST handler — even with timeout=10 this can add up to 10s latency to a message send when Resend is misconfigured. Since the try/except wrapper catches the exception, this is OK in preview (RESEND_API_KEY empty short-circuits inside send_html_email), but for production consider asyncio.create_task to fire-and-forget instead of awaiting.

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (bubble panel / admin SEND blocked by preview overlay only)

seed_data_creation: Created 3 support threads via tests (one admin closed). Messages + 1 PNG attachment uploaded. All test data lives in support_threads / support_messages collections.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_iter26_support.py as the regression file (uses session-scoped admin_token + fresh registered users via the shared conftest.user_a/user_b pattern but defines its own support_user_a/_b). Preview env's Emergent badge at viewport bottom-right z-index can hide the support bubble and admin SEND button — use force=True click in Playwright tests against /app and /admin/support.
rca of the issue: Floating bubble panel did not visually open in playwright with natural-coordinate click because document.elementFromPoint(bubble center) returned the Emergent preview badge anchor (#emergent-badge id), not the support button. With page.click(..., force=True) the bubble onClick handler does fire (verified setState toggles); however, on the admin /admin/support page the SEND button bounding box also sits underneath the badge so a natural click is consumed by the badge. This is a preview-env artifact — fixable in product by either raising z-index above the badge (badge is likely z-index ~9999) or shifting the bubble away from bottom-right (e.g., bottom-6 right-24). Backend send / inbox functionality verified directly via pytest with 100% pass rate.
